questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.question: A spinning dancer rotates faster when she pulls her outstretched arms close to her body. This happens because of the conservation of:
questions.explanation: With no external torque, Iω stays constant. Pulling the arms in lowers I, so ω must rise. Her kinetic energy actually increases, using muscular work.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 6: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two tuning forks of frequencies 256 Hz and 260 Hz are sounded together. The number of beats heard per second is:
questions.explanation: Beat frequency is the difference of the two frequencies, 260 - 256 = 4 beats per second.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An electric dipole placed in a uniform external electric field experiences:
options: A net force but no torque
A torque but no net force
Both a net force and a torque
Neither a force nor a torque
questions.explanation: The equal and opposite forces on the two charges cancel, so the net force is zero, but they form a couple giving torque τ = pE sin θ.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 12, Chapter 1: Electric Charges and Fields

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following molecules has polar bonds but a zero net dipole moment?
questions.explanation: CO₂ is linear and symmetrical, so the two equal C=O bond dipoles point opposite ways and cancel. Water and ammonia are bent and pyramidal, so theirs do not.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 11, Chapter 4: Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to the Bronsted-Lowry concept, the conjugate base of H₂PO₄⁻ is:
questions.explanation: A conjugate base is what remains after one proton is donated, so H₂PO₄⁻ loses H⁺ to give HPO₄²⁻. Adding a proton would instead give the conjugate acid H₃PO₄.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The Cannizzaro reaction is given only by those aldehydes which:
options: Contain at least one alpha hydrogen
questions.explanation: Aldehydes without an alpha hydrogen, such as HCHO and benzaldehyde, cannot undergo aldol condensation and instead disproportionate with strong alkali.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 12, Chapter 8: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: In dicotyledonous leaves, the guard cells surrounding a stoma are:
options: Bean or kidney shaped with unevenly thickened walls
questions.explanation: The inner wall facing the pore is thick and the outer wall thin, so when the cells become turgid they bend outwards and the stoma opens. Grasses have dumb-bell shaped guard cells.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 6: Anatomy of Flowering Plants

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The cuckoo (koel) laying its eggs in a crow's nest so that the crow raises its young is an example of:
questions.explanation: In brood parasitism the parasitic bird gets its offspring reared by the host, and its eggs have evolved to resemble the host's in size and colour.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 11: Organisms and Populations

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The first heart sound, lubb, is produced by the closure of the:
questions.explanation: Lubb marks the closure of the bicuspid and tricuspid valves at the start of ventricular systole; dup is the later closure of the semilunar valves.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 15: Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: A non-protein organic cofactor that remains tightly bound to the enzyme throughout the reaction is called a:
questions.explanation: Prosthetic groups such as the haem of peroxidase stay firmly attached, while coenzymes like NAD bind only transiently during catalysis.
